svg.title: Net Revenue Interest From Lessee to Pooled Owner
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-nri-decimal-comparison; chapter number: 4; title: Net Revenue Interest From Lessee to Pooled Owner; subtitle: How royalties, overrides and pooling carve the decimal; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 0.001875 to 0.875 net revenue interest; buckets: label: Lessee NRI under a 1/8 lease; low: 0.875; high: 0.875; notes: 100% WI after the lease, less the 1/8 royalty (Alyce Hoge drills).; label: Lessee NRI under a 3/16 lease; low: 0.8125; high: 0.8125; notes: A higher royalty leaves less for the operator before any override or NPRI.; label: Sunrise lease pooled into a 320-acre unit; low: 0.20625; high: 0.825; notes: 82.5 cents per dollar after a 12.5% royalty and 5% override, then 0.20625 once 80 acres are pooled into 320.; label: Bakken owner in a 1,280-acre DSU; low: 0.001875; high: 0.001875; notes: 16 NMA divided by 1,280 times 15%. About $937 on 10,000 barrels at $50 over three months.; caption: Every division-order decimal is built by multiplication. Run the check and balance lease by lease, and challenge the operator when your number does not match.; assumptions note: Each bucket is a separate worked example, not one shared property. Sands notes Bakken barrels bring $50 against $60 WTI because of the price differential.; note: Attributed to Matt Sands (Yy7az5T7_vs), Land Training www.landtraining.net (eZU5hvGcngg) and UHD Continuing and Professional Education (oHKF06pFkh0) on YouTube.
